correctness.rationale: A vector in a simplex factor has unique barycentric increments b_j summing to zero. Membership in t(Δ−Δ) is equivalent to Σ(b_j)_+≤t by taking the positive and negative parts and filling both with the same nonnegative mass. The overlap constraints are z_j≥max(0,b_j), Σz_j=1, hence the overlap volume fraction is (1−Σ(b_j)_+)^d (zero at tangency). The two signs of the translation give the same volume. Uniform product measure and convexity now give the directional survival product, or equivalently the minimum of independent scaled Beta(1,d_i) variables, omitting zero blocks. The difference-body gauge is the maximum factor gauge a, so after multiplying the exit time by a, at least one normalized gauge is 1. On 0<t<1 each survival factor is at least (1−t)^{d_i}; a maximal-gauge factor bounds the product above by (1−t)^δ. In each case non-equality gives strict inequality throughout that interval: the lower equality requires every normalized gauge to be 1; the upper equality requires one active factor of dimension δ. The polynomial survival on [0,1] has bounded density with no endpoint atoms, giving integrable logs and finite moments for p>−1. Strict stochastic order therefore gives strict power-mean order, including p<0 where the sign is reversed twice, and strict logarithmic-mean order at p=0. Beta integration and the derivative at zero give the stated constants. Both contact types exist for every fixed product. For the ratio, log(1+p/j)/p=∫_0^1 (j+pv)^(−1) dv, continuous at p=0 and strictly decreasing in p. At −1 the sum over j>δ telescopes to log(D/δ), and at positive infinity it tends to zero. With D=2N and δ=N the sum is a Riemann sum for (1/λ)∫_1^2 log(1+λ/t)dt if p_N/N→λ>0; the uniform expansion for p_N=o(N) and the bound (N/p_N)log(1+p_N/N) for p_N/N→∞ give the other limits, including p_N=0 or negative on the small-parameter side. This verifies the contact and limit claims with the intrinsic gauge, not Euclidean radii.
residual_risks: Packaged code was inspected, not executed. Its reported 4,230 test cases check exact finite moment identities and finite numerical comparisons, not the universal sharpness or crossover.

Exact spot-check replay: at p=1 with dimensions (2,3) and normalized gauges (1,1/2), integrate (1−t)²(1−t/2)³ over [0,1], obtaining 37/160 strictly between 1/6 and 1/3. The polynomial overlap and stochastic comparison, not finite checks, establish the full result.

value.rationale: This answers the geometric problem of how much the intrinsic radial-mean radius varies with direction for a fixed product rather than bounding it uniformly over an unrelated class. The worst and best directions behave differently: synchronization across every factor gives the inner contact, while complete concentration in a smallest-dimensional factor gives the outer contact. That sharp dichotomy and the complete crossover at p of order N show how dimension and exponent compete in anisotropy even when the shapes of the simplices vary. The value is in the joint sharp classification and asymptotic regime, not the already covered lower inclusion or factorization as a standalone formula.
residual_risks: The asymptotic crossover is proved only for the balanced two-factor family; the theorem does not provide a universal outer bound for arbitrary bodies or optimize the comparison up to linear transformations.
